title: Hosted API surge token-econ response plan
body:
Purpose
---
Quick-response working doc and spreadsheet snapshot to (1) model per-1k-token COGS across models/regions during traffic surges, (2) recommend immediate mitigations we can toggle from Console, and (3) provide conservative savings estimates for exec + SRE triage. This is a working doc — numbers are conservative estimates derived from infra cost models and recent host usage telemetry.

Assumptions (global)
- All cost figures expressed per 1,000 tokens (per-1k). We use 1k-token buckets to avoid tiny decimals.
- GPU runtime cost = effective amortized GPU hourly + energy + infra overhead converted to per-1k via observed throughput for that model/sequence length distribution.
- Network egress and storage for KV cache counted where relevant.
- Burst period defined as 10x baseline QPS sustained for 15 minutes.
- Fallback variants: quantized or smaller architecture we can route to when capacity constrained.

Key immediate goals
- Avoid catastrophic margin collapse in an unplanned surge while keeping SLAs acceptable for paying customers.
- Identify toggles we can flip from Console within 5 minutes (routing policy, quantization fallback, regional re-routing, short-response mode).
- Provide quick P&L snapshots to CS/Finance for customer communications.

Spreadsheet snapshot: per-1k-token COGS matrix (sample)

Notes on the table
- GPU per-1k numbers reflect surge adjustments: during a surge effective per-1k GPU cost increases because throughput per GPU can drop (smaller packing, more tail latency), and we show a 10–20% uplift in the region with less spare capacity.
- Infra amort includes reserved instance amortization and per-request orchestration overhead.
- List Price is an example routing price for hosted API; pricing is region-agnostic in this snapshot but can be mapped to regional ratecards.

Surge scenarios modelled (short descriptions)
- Scenario A: 10x short spike (15 min), origin US-EAST heavy (70% of spike).
- Scenario B: Regional failure in EU (downtime 5 min) causing EU->US traffic redirection maintaining 80% of EU traffic.
- Scenario C: Sustained surge (1h) with 3x baseline across all regions (capacity stress) requiring fallback routing.

Per-scenario quick calculations (example outputs)
- Scenario A, redwood-alpha-13b, us-east: baseline per-1k GPU=1.02 -> surge uplift to 1.12 (+9.8%). If 40% of traffic can be routed to quantized variant (gpt-j-7b-quant) avg. COGS falls from 1.31 -> 1.00 per-1k (approx 24% saving) assuming no change in pricing. If we enable burst reserved capacity (paid commit amortized), net uplift is limited to +3% instead of +10%.
- Scenario B, eu-west failover: egress costs increase for EU-origin requests routed to US by ~0.02–0.05 per-1k; latency-sensitive customers should be routed to EU-fallback models if available.

Console toggles and response playbook (ordered)
1) Enable quantized fallback routing (Console toggle: "fallback_quantized" -> true). Effect: immediate ~20–30% per-1k GPU reduction for redirected traffic; risk: small quality delta for some prompts. Owner: Product Ops (Priya). ETA: <5 min to enable.
2) Regional ingress throttling for anonymous/free-tier traffic (Console policy: ingress-rate-limit: free-tier -> 50% throttle). Effect: reduces noise load during surge, preserves capacity for paid routes. Owner: Growth Ops (Laura). ETA: 3–10 min.
3) Burst reserved allocation (if available) — convert short-term on-demand to prepaid burst pools. Effect: reduces per-1k uplift to single-digit. Requires finance approval for immediate commit. Owner: Finance (Omar). ETA: 30–120 min.
4) Short-response mode (truncate generation early for best-effort traffic) — create 'fast-mode' routing that caps max_tokens or uses aggressive decoding settings. Effect: immediate token demand reduction up to 35% for specific endpoints. Risk: user-visible quality loss. Owner: Eng-runway. ETA: 10 min to flip for specific routes.
5) Regional re-pricing for burst windows (billing side) — temporary surcharge for heavy non-SLA traffic to protect margin. Effect: preserves revenue/margin; requires CS communications. Owner: Pricing/Product. ETA: 45–90 min.

Conservative savings estimates (back-of-envelope)
- Combined quantized fallback + free-tier throttle in a US-heavy 10x spike: per-1k net COGS reduction = 24% -> if we reduce exposed paid volume by 40% to cheaper variant and throttle 30% of non-paying traffic, net platform COGS saving = ~18–22% during spike window.
- If we deploy burst-reserved commit before planned Black Friday-like events, incremental unit cost during peak can be reduced to ~5–8% over baseline vs on-demand 10–25% uplift.

Short checklist for on-call SRE / Product Ops
- [ ] Confirm customer SLAs impacted list (auto-populate from incident page).
- [ ] Flip fallback_quantized for non-whitelisted customers.
- [ ] Apply free-tier/guest-rate limit rule.
- [ ] Notify CS + send templated customer comms for enterprise customers (JIRA-7982).
- [ ] If surge persists beyond 30 min, propose burst reserve purchase and open Finance approval.

Open questions / follow-ups
- Need a quick A/B eval dataset for redwood-alpha-13b -> gpt-j-7b-quant quality delta for chat flows (owner: Applied ML).
- Can Console expose a single-click "surge-mode" that sequences the 5 toggles above? (owner: Console PM).
- How fast can billing apply regional temporary re-pricing without manual intervention? (owner: Billing infra).

Appendix: sample micro-sim inputs used for the table (for reproducibility)
- Baseline QPS per model: alpha-13b: 120 qps (us-east strong), opt-70b: 18 qps, gpt-j-7b-quant: 60 qps.
- Avg tokens per request: 420 (chat style).
- GPU effective throughput assumptions: alpha-13b: 380k tokens per GPU/hr (normal), 330k tokens per GPU/hr (surge small-packing). opt-70b-8bit: 200k normal, 160k surge. gpt-j-7b-quant: 850k normal, 760k surge.

Action items (owners + due dates)
- Priya Desai: implement console toggle for fallback_quantized and test in staging (due 2026-02-28).
- Laura Chen: draft free-tier surge throttle rules and comms (due 2026-03-03).
- Omar Farouk: scope burst-reserved short-term commit and estimate immediate budget (due 2026-03-05).
- Applied ML (TBD): provide quick eval comparing top 50 prompts between alpha-13b and gpt-j-7b-quant (due 2026-03-06).

Versioning note
This is a working doc; when toggles go live we snapshot the spreadsheet as a released 'surge-runbook-v1' and attach to the incident. For now mark this doc as 'in_review' and update the table with actual telemetry numbers post-incident.
